title: A high‐resolution system for dual observations of oxygen dynamics and meiofauna behavior in aquatic sediments
content:
Abstract

Meiofauna play a critical role for detrital food web structures, benthic element cycling and biodiversity in aquatic sediments. Most taxa are aerobic and are expected to mainly inhabit oxic sediments, but some taxa appear to endure prolonged hypoxic and anoxic conditions. We still have very limited insights on migration patterns, micro scale distribution and behavior of meiofauna in intact surficial sediments—which must have major implications for bioturbation and the biogeochemical function of sediments. Here, we present a novel experimental system that maps real time oxygen distribution at high spatial resolution along with the movements of meiofauna using self-developed machine-learning-based tracking approaches. We showcased how our novel setup can resolve the distribution and behavioral responses of nematodes exposed to changing oxygen conditions with high sensitivity. The studied nematodes congregated along the oxygen penetration depth (OPD) and clearly preferred being present in strongly oxygen depleted environments, efficiently following the advancing or receding OPD, but becoming inactive in anoxia. Our systems demonstrated the ability to resolve such meiofaunal behavior in high sensitivity, which must have important implications for solute and solid mixing and biogeochemical processing, in dynamic coastal sediments.
